//overrides: An override is a standing instruction to ignore what a dependency asked for, so each entry states the advisory it answers and the condition that retires it. Retirement is measured by REMOVING the entry and re-running npm audit, not by reasoning about version numbers (T-165). js-yaml (T-196, GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj): @redocly/openapi-core 1.34.18 pins js-yaml 4.3.0 and the advisory covers 4.0.0-4.3.0; reached only through the openapi-typescript devDependency, which generates lib/api-types.ts and ships nothing. Drop it when @redocly pins >4.3.0. The 4.x line is deliberate: 5.x exists and is a major @redocly does not declare support for, and trading a known advisory for an unknown break in the toolchain that generates the typed contract is the wrong trade. RETIRED 2026-08-11 by T-165, when next 16.2.12 -> 16.3.0 moved postcss 8.4.31 -> 8.5.23 and sharp ^0.34.5 -> ^0.35.3, both clear of their advisories: postcss (T-152), sharp (T-152), and nanoid (T-196) - the last of which existed only because the postcss override had pulled a newer postcss that carried it, an override answering an override's own side effect.
